title: Focused Cavity Resonance Scan with Mirror Step Constraints
scientific_hypothesis: The defect cavity thickness near 381nm is the primary determinant of 1550nm transmission peak position and bandwidth; fine-tuning this layer while constraining mirror adjustments will improve target score without degrading visible reflectance.
design_principle: Initialize from top-3 candidates from previous batch, apply deterministic ±6nm perturbation grid to defect layer 10 (centered on ~381.5nm), constrain optimizer step sizes for mirror layers 0-9 and 11-20 to 20% of current magnitude to prevent destructive mirror-detuning.
proposed_topology: 21-layer stack: (HfO2/SiO2)×5 mirror | HfO2 cavity layer | (SiO2/HfO2)×5 mirror on fused silica substrate, air incident
design_variables: All 21 layer thicknesses with cavity layer ±6nm perturbation grid
Mirror layer optimizer step size constrained to 20%
manufacturing_considerations: Cavity thickness precision critical for resonance
theory_basis: Fabry-Perot cavity resonance condition determines passband center wavelength
Mirror layers primarily control stopband reflectance and bandwidth
expected_advantages: Preserves mirror phase contributions while tuning cavity resonance
May identify local optimum near previous best candidates
known_risks: ±6nm window may not contain global optimum
Step size constraints may slow convergence
Mirror-cavity coupling effects may be underestimated
execution_request_english: Design a 21-layer HfO2/SiO2 defect-cavity filter on fused silica substrate with air incident medium. Stack sequence: HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2(cavity)|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2. Initialize optimization from three candidate thickness sets: candidate A [250.6, 306.5, 256.0, 300.9, 269.6, 278.7, 239.9, 252.1, 231.9, 290.2, 382.8, 252.6, 223.5, 252.2, 327.5, 235.6, 255.1, 324.4, 300.3, 253.3, 229.1] nm, candidate B [251.0, 336.4, 257.0, 332.3, 272.2, 284.3, 325.0, 266.3, 305.3, 263.6, 382.1, 269.8, 247.9, 285.2, 315.0, 248.1, 245.0, 277.8, 240.9, 263.8, 255.9] nm, candidate C [334.9, 266.1, 224.5, 253.9, 325.4, 247.8, 234.8, 315.2, 244.8, 263.9, 381.3, 243.2, 265.8, 280.5, 281.2, 322.1, 259.2, 283.0, 255.5, 327.4, 283.8] nm. Apply deterministic perturbation grid to layer 10 (cavity): test thicknesses at [375.5, 379.5, 381.5, 383.5, 387.5] nm. Constrain L-BFGS-B optimizer step sizes for layers 0-9 and 11-20 to maximum 20% of their current thickness values per iteration. Evaluate at normal incidence, unpolarized or both TE/TM. Optimize for high transmittance in 1530-1565nm band and high reflectance in 400-700nm band. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 1530-1565 nm, 400-700 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band; High reflectance in 400-700 nm band. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Low reflectance in 1530-1565 nm band; Low transmittance in 400-700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: Maximum 30 layers.
revision_reason: Follows feedback directive to clone top-3 candidates and apply ±6nm perturbation grid to defect layer 10 while constraining mirror layer optimizer steps to 20% magnitude. Execution request repaired to be fully standalone without referencing prior route.
